questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. One nanometre is equal to 10^-6 metre.
2. Nanomaterials are generally those having at least one dimension in the range of about 1 to 100 nanometres.
3. At the nanoscale, properties such as colour, melting point and electrical conductivity can differ from those of the same material in bulk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: One nanometre is 10^-9 metre, and 10^-6 metre is a micrometre. The range of 1 to 100 nm is the working definition because below this size quantum and surface effects begin to change properties.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Statement-I: As the size of a particle decreases, its surface area to volume ratio decreases.
Statement-II: In smaller particles a larger fraction of the atoms lies on the surface.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Shrinking a particle increases its surface area relative to its volume, so Statement-I is wrong. Because more atoms sit on the surface, nanoparticles are more reactive and make good catalysts, which makes Statement-II correct.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Discovery of the fullerene C60
2. Richard Feynman's talk 'There's Plenty of Room at the Bottom'
3. Isolation of graphene
4. Coining of the term 'nanotechnology' by Norio Taniguchi
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Feynman's talk was in 1959, Taniguchi coined the term in 1974, the fullerene was found in 1985 and graphene was isolated in 2004. The ideas thus came long before the material discoveries.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about microscopes used for nanoscale studies:
1. The scanning tunnelling microscope works on the quantum tunnelling of electrons between a sharp tip and the sample surface.
2. The scanning tunnelling microscope can image any sample, including non-conducting ones such as plastics, without special preparation.
3. The atomic force microscope senses the force between a tip and the surface and can image non-conducting samples.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The STM needs a conducting or semiconducting surface because it measures tunnelling current. The AFM measures force, so it works on insulating materials as well.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Electron microscopes can resolve details far finer than optical microscopes because:
o: the wavelength of the electrons used is much shorter than that of visible light
electrons carry more charge than photons and so scatter more strongly
they use lenses made of larger glass diameters
they magnify the image by a larger optical factor using several eyepieces
questions.e: Resolution is limited by the wavelength of the probing radiation, and fast electrons have wavelengths of a fraction of a nanometre against several hundred nanometres for visible light. TEM and SEM both use this advantage.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics, Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the fullerene C60:
1. Its molecule resembles a football, with 12 pentagonal and 20 hexagonal faces.
2. Its discoverers, Kroto, Curl and Smalley, received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1996.
3. It is a flat, single-layer sheet of carbon atoms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A flat single layer of carbon atoms is graphene, not a fullerene; C60 is a closed cage that is called buckminsterfullerene. Hence statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Chemistry, The p-Block Elements; Nobel Prize 1996

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about carbon nanotubes:
1. They can be viewed as rolled-up sheets of graphene.
2. On the basis of weight, their tensile strength is much greater than that of steel.
3. Depending on how the sheet is rolled (chirality), a nanotube can behave as a metal or as a semiconductor.
4. All single-walled carbon nanotubes are electrical insulators.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 to 3 are correct. Chirality decides the electronic character, which is why nanotubes are studied for both wiring and transistors, and so the claim that all of them are insulators is wrong.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about graphene:
1. It is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
2. Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2010 for work on it.
3. It is a wide band gap semiconductor like silicon carbide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Graphene is a zero band gap material with excellent conduction, which makes it hard to use directly as a switch in digital transistors. Hence statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2010 (Physics); NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Fullerene : Kroto, Curl and Smalley
2. Carbon nanotubes : Andre Geim
3. Graphene : Geim and Novoselov
4. Scanning tunnelling microscope : Ernst Ruska
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Carbon nanotubes are credited to Sumio Iijima (1991), and the scanning tunnelling microscope to Binnig and Rohrer, while Ruska is associated with the electron microscope.
questions.s: Nobel Prize announcements; DST Nano Mission

questions.q: As the size of a semiconductor quantum dot is reduced, the colour of the light it emits shifts towards:
o: the red end of the spectrum
the infrared region, without any visible emission
no change, since colour depends only on the material
the blue end of the spectrum
questions.e: Smaller dots confine electrons more strongly, which widens the band gap and gives shorter-wavelength (bluer) light. Larger dots of the same material emit redder light. The 2023 Nobel Prize in Chemistry honoured Bawendi, Brus and Ekimov for quantum dots.
questions.s: Nobel Prize 2023 (Chemistry); NCERT Class XII Physics

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quantum dots:
1. They are used as fluorescent labels for imaging in biology.
2. Many of them contain cadmium, which raises toxicity concerns.
3. The colour of light emitted by a quantum dot is independent of its size.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Their size-tunable bright emission suits bio-imaging and display screens, but cadmium-based dots can be toxic. Size determines the emission colour, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Which one of the following is a 'bottom-up' approach to making nanomaterials?
o: Chemical vapour deposition, in which carbon atoms assemble into nanotubes on a catalyst
Ball milling of a bulk metal into fine powder
Photolithography to etch patterns on a silicon wafer
Mechanical grinding of a bulk crystal into small particles
questions.e: Bottom-up methods build structures from atoms or molecules, as in chemical vapour deposition, sol-gel and self-assembly. Milling, grinding and lithographic etching start from bulk and remove material, which is the top-down route.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry
questions.h: Top-down = carve a statue; Bottom-up = build with bricks

questions.q: Nanoparticles of which metal are widely used as antimicrobial agents in wound dressings and some water filters?
questions.e: Silver ions released from nanoparticles damage microbial cell membranes and enzymes. The large surface area helps release more ions, but there is also concern about silver entering the environment.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Which of the following nanoparticles are used in sunscreens as transparent blockers of ultraviolet radiation?
questions.e: At the nanoscale, titanium dioxide and zinc oxide still absorb and scatter UV light but no longer scatter visible light, so the cream does not leave a white film. Safety of nanoparticle sunscreens on broken skin is still debated.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Statement-I: Colloidal gold nanoparticles can appear red or purple, although bulk gold is yellow.
Statement-II: The colour of gold nanoparticles depends on their size and shape because of surface plasmon resonance.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The free electrons on the nanoparticle surface oscillate together at a frequency set by particle size and shape, so they absorb different colours. This principle is used in lateral flow tests such as home pregnancy kits.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Chemistry, Surface Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nanotechnology in medicine:
1. Lipid nanoparticles were used to deliver mRNA in some COVID-19 vaccines.
2. Nanocarriers can accumulate in tumours because tumour blood vessels are leaky (the enhanced permeability and retention effect).
3. Nanoparticles can never cross any biological barrier in the body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The lipid shell protects the fragile mRNA and helps it enter cells. Some nanoparticles can cross barriers, such as the blood-brain barrier, which is both a promise for drug delivery and a toxicity concern.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles are being researched for which of the following uses?
o: As transparent UV blockers in cosmetics
As the active material of solid-state lasers
As contrast agents in MRI and for magnetic hyperthermia treatment of tumours
questions.e: Iron oxide nanoparticles respond to an external magnetic field and can be heated by an alternating field to kill tumour cells. The other uses involve TiO2 or ZnO, laser crystals and microbes, respectively.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nano urea:
1. Nano urea in liquid form was developed by IFFCO.
2. It is applied as a foliar spray on plant leaves.
3. It is a granular solid fertiliser that is mixed into the soil before sowing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nano urea is a liquid with nanoscale nitrogen particles sprayed on the leaves, which have a large surface area for uptake. It was meant to reduce the use of conventional bagged urea and cut losses by leaching and volatilisation.
questions.s: PIB; IFFCO

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Nano Mission:
1. It is an umbrella programme of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.
2. It was launched in 2007.
3. The Institute of Nano Science and Technology, Mohali is an autonomous institute under the Department of Science and Technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Nano Mission is run by the Department of Science and Technology (Ministry of Science and Technology), not MeitY. INST Mohali, an autonomous DST institute, is a hub for nano research.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding risks of nanomaterials:
1. Because of their tiny size, some nanoparticles can enter cells and travel in the body.
2. Long, rigid carbon nanotubes have raised concerns of lung injury similar to that caused by asbestos fibres.
3. Nanomaterials are always chemically inert and safe because the bulk form of the same material is safe.
4. Nanoparticles released into water cannot affect aquatic organisms.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Bulk safety does not guarantee nanoscale safety, since surface reactivity and size change behaviour, and nanoparticles such as silver can harm aquatic life.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Statement-I: Water droplets roll off a lotus leaf, carrying dirt with them.
Statement-II: A water droplet placed on a lotus leaf spreads out and wets its surface completely.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The leaf has micro and nanoscale bumps coated with wax, which makes the surface superhydrophobic, so droplets stay as beads and roll away. This lotus effect has inspired self-cleaning paints and fabrics.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Nanoscale zero-valent iron particles are being studied for:
o: increasing the nitrogen content of fertilisers
remediation of groundwater contaminated with chlorinated solvents and heavy metals
storing hydrogen in fuel cell vehicles
questions.e: Iron is a reducing agent, and in nano form its large surface area makes it react fast with pollutants such as chlorinated solvents and some metals in groundwater. Their release without control is itself a concern.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: 'Green synthesis' of nanoparticles refers to:
o: making nanoparticles using plant extracts, bacteria or fungi instead of harsh chemicals
making nanoparticles only in outer space without gravity
using toxic reducing agents such as sodium borohydride
making only those nanoparticles that are green in colour
questions.e: Biomolecules in plant extracts or microbes can reduce metal ions and also cap the particles, which avoids toxic reagents and so is called environmentally friendly.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Nanoclay added to a polymer for food packaging is mainly intended to:
o: make the film an electrical conductor
make the film dissolve quickly in water
improve the barrier against gases and moisture and strengthen the film
questions.e: Platelets of nanoclay create a tortuous path for gas and water vapour molecules, so food stays fresh longer. Such nanocomposites also raise questions about migration of nanoparticles into food.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q: Self-cleaning glass coated with nanoparticles of titanium dioxide works mainly because:
o: it repels all water completely and so prevents dust from sticking
it conducts heat away and thereby melts dust
under sunlight it breaks down organic dirt by photocatalysis and spreads water into a film that washes the dirt away
it magnetically attracts dust into the frame
questions.e: Titanium dioxide acts as a photocatalyst under ultraviolet light, decomposing organic deposits, and the surface becomes hydrophilic so water sheets off and carries the loosened dirt.
questions.s: DST Nano Mission; NCERT Class XII Chemistry

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about patents in India:
1. A patent is granted for a term of 20 years from the date of filing of the application.
2. Product patents for pharmaceuticals, food and chemicals were reintroduced by the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2005.
3. The term of a patent is 14 years from the date of grant.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 20-year term runs from filing, not from grant, and was fixed by the Patents (Amendment) Act 2002 to match TRIPS. The 2005 amendment ended the earlier regime that allowed only process patents for drugs.
questions.s: Patents Act, 1970; DPIIT

questions.q: In Novartis AG v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court refused a patent for the beta crystalline form of imatinib mesylate (Glivec) because:
o: India does not grant patents on pharmaceutical products
the drug was already under a compulsory licence
it was a new form of a known substance without enhanced therapeutic efficacy, as required by Section 3(d)
the court held that TRIPS prohibits patents on cancer drugs
questions.e: Section 3(d) was added in 2005 to check the 'evergreening' of patents. It bars patents for new forms of known substances unless they show significantly enhanced efficacy.
questions.s: Novartis AG v. Union of India (2013); Patents Act, 1970, Sec 3(d)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about what is excluded from patentability under the Patents Act, 1970:
1. A computer programme per se.
2. Plants and animals in whole or in part, other than micro-organisms.
3. Micro-organisms, which cannot be patented in any form.
4. A method of agriculture or horticulture.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct, being listed in Section 3. Micro-organisms are not excluded, and the TRIPS agreement also requires that they be patentable.
questions.s: Patents Act, 1970, Section 3

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about compulsory licensing in India:
1. The first compulsory licence in India was granted in 2012 to Natco Pharma for Bayer's cancer drug sorafenib (Nexavar).
2. An application for a compulsory licence can be made only by the Government, not by a private party.
3. An application can be made after three years from the grant of the patent, on grounds such as the invention not being available at a reasonably affordable price.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Section 84 any person interested may apply after three years from grant. The Natco case is the standard example of the ground of unaffordable price.
questions.s: Patents Act, 1970, Sec 84; Controller of Patents order, 2012

questions.q:
Statement-I: In India, a generic manufacturer may use a patented drug for experiments needed to obtain regulatory approval before the patent expires.
Statement-II: Section 107A of the Patents Act, 1970 provides an exemption for acts done solely for uses reasonably related to the development and submission of information required by law.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: This is the Bolar provision, named after a US case. It lets generics be launched on the day the patent expires, and Section 107A is the legal basis for the permission.
questions.s: Patents Act, 1970, Sec 107A

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about copyright in India:
1. Copyright protects the expression of ideas and not the ideas themselves.
2. Registration is compulsory for a work to enjoy copyright protection.
3. For literary works, copyright generally lasts for the lifetime of the author plus 60 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Copyright arises automatically on creation of an original work, and registration only serves as evidence. India follows the Berne Convention, which does not allow formalities as a condition of protection.
questions.s: Copyright Act, 1957; Berne Convention

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Computer programmes are protected as literary works under the Copyright Act, 1957.
2. If an author assigns the copyright in a work, the author's moral rights also pass to the assignee.
3. Cinematograph films are not eligible for copyright protection.
4. Fair dealing for purposes such as private study, research, criticism or review is not an infringement.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Moral rights of paternity and integrity stay with the author even after assignment (Section 57), and films are a category of work protected under the Act.
questions.s: Copyright Act, 1957, Sec 2(o), 52, 57

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about trade marks in India:
1. A registered trade mark is valid for 20 years and cannot be renewed.
2. India acceded to the Madrid Protocol in 2013, allowing international registration of marks through a single application.
3. The shape of goods and combinations of colours can be registered as trade marks if they are distinctive.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Registration lasts 10 years and can be renewed for further periods of 10 years indefinitely, as long as fees are paid. That is the main difference from a patent, which expires.
questions.s: Trade Marks Act, 1999; DPIIT

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Geographical Indications (GI) in India:
1. The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999 came into force in 2003.
2. Basmati rice was the first product to be registered as a GI in India.
3. A registered GI is valid for 20 years and cannot be renewed.
4. The Geographical Indications Registry is located at Chennai.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Darjeeling tea was the first GI in India, and a GI registration is valid for 10 years and can be renewed.
questions.s: GI Act, 1999; DPIIT / GI Registry

questions.q:
Statement-I: A registered Geographical Indication in India cannot be assigned, licensed or mortgaged in the way a trade mark can.
Statement-II: A Geographical Indication is a collective right of the producers of a particular region and not the property of one individual.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Section 24 of the GI Act bars assignment, transmission, licensing or pledging because the right belongs to the community of producers of that place. This collective character explains why it cannot be sold off to a single owner.
questions.s: GI Act, 1999, Sec 24

questions.q:
Match List-I (GI product) with List-II (State):
A. Muga silk
B. Kanchipuram silk
C. Bikaneri bhujia
D. Nagpur orange
1. Rajasthan
2. Maharashtra
3. Assam
4. Tamil Nadu
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Muga silk is golden silk from Assam, Kanchipuram silk is from Tamil Nadu, Bikaneri bhujia is from the Bikaner region of Rajasthan, and Nagpur orange is from Maharashtra.
questions.s: GI Registry, DPIIT

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the TRIPS Agreement:
1. It sets minimum standards of protection for intellectual property rights for members of the WTO.
2. It is administered by the World Intellectual Property Organization.
3. It requires members to protect plant varieties either by patents or by an effective sui generis system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: TRIPS came into force in 1995 and is administered by the WTO, not WIPO, which is a UN specialised agency that administers treaties like Berne and Paris. India chose a sui generis system for plants.
questions.s: WTO TRIPS Agreement, Art 27.3(b)

questions.q: India met its TRIPS obligation relating to the protection of plant varieties through the:
o: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001
questions.e: TRIPS lets members protect plant varieties by patents or by an effective sui generis system, and India chose the latter. The PPVFR Act protects breeders as well as farmers.
questions.s: PPVFR Act, 2001; TRIPS Art 27.3(b)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act, 2001:
1. A farmer may save, use, sow, exchange, share or sell the farm produce of a protected variety, except branded seed.
2. Breeders' rights last 25 years for all crops.
3. Farmers' varieties can also be registered under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act recognises the farmer as both a cultivator and a breeder. Breeders' rights last 15 years for most crops and 18 years for trees and vines, not 25.
questions.s: PPVFR Act, 2001

questions.q: The Doha Declaration on the TRIPS Agreement and Public Health (2001) affirmed that:
o: countries must withdraw all patents on medicines within five years
TRIPS does not prevent members from taking measures to protect public health, including the use of compulsory licences
developing countries must adopt 30-year patents on medicines
compulsory licences are allowed only for pandemics declared by the WHO
questions.e: It was a response to the concerns about access to HIV drugs and clarified the flexibilities in TRIPS. Each member has the freedom to determine the grounds for granting compulsory licences.
questions.s: WTO Doha Declaration, 2001

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Berne Convention : Protection of literary and artistic works
2. Paris Convention : Protection of industrial property
3. Budapest Treaty : International recognition of the deposit of micro-organisms for patent procedure
4. Patent Cooperation Treaty : Filing a single international application for patents in many countries
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: All four pairs are correct. These are the foundational treaties administered by WIPO, and India is a party to each of them.
questions.s: WIPO treaties; India Year Book

questions.q: The Marrakesh Treaty, 2013, administered by WIPO, is meant to:
o: protect new varieties of plants bred by plant breeders
regulate the transboundary movement of living modified organisms
facilitate access to published works for persons who are blind, visually impaired or otherwise print disabled
questions.e: It creates an exception to copyright so that works can be converted into accessible formats such as Braille and audio. India was among the first to ratify it, in 2014.
questions.s: WIPO; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Intellectual Property Rights Policy, 2016:
1. Its tagline is 'Creative India; Innovative India'.
2. The nodal department for IPR is the Ministry of Science and Technology.
3. It led to the setting up of the Cell for IPR Promotion and Management (CIPAM).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The DPIIT in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry is the nodal department for IPR, and CIPAM works under it. Science and Technology is not the nodal ministry.
questions.s: PIB, May 2016; DPIIT

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 and IPR:
1. Prior approval of the National Biodiversity Authority is required before applying for an IPR in India or abroad for an invention based on a biological resource obtained from India.
2. The National Biodiversity Authority is headquartered at Chennai.
3. The National Biodiversity Authority functions under the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 6 aims to stop biopiracy. The NBA is a statutory body under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
questions.s: Biological Diversity Act, 2002, Sec 6; Shankar IAS Environment

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the protection of India's traditional knowledge:
1. The United States patent on the wound-healing use of turmeric was revoked after a challenge by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
2. A patent on a fungicidal use of neem granted by the European Patent Office was revoked on challenge.
3. The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library is maintained by the World Intellectual Property Organization.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The TKDL was created by CSIR and the Ministry of AYUSH to record traditional knowledge in patent-friendly languages, and it is used by patent examiners as prior art. WIPO does not maintain it.
questions.s: Shankar IAS Environment; CSIR

questions.q:
Statement-I: India has no dedicated statute for the protection of trade secrets.
Statement-II: Trade secrets in India are protected through contract law and the equitable principle of breach of confidence.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true, but II describes the substitute remedies rather than giving the reason why there is no statute. Courts enforce confidentiality agreements and grant injunctions against misuse of confidential information.
questions.s: India Year Book; DPIIT

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Intellectual Property Appellate Board (IPAB) is correct?
o: It was dissolved in 2021 under the Tribunals Reforms Act, and its appellate work passed mainly to the High Courts
It was set up under the TRIPS Agreement to hear disputes between countries
It still hears appeals on patents, trade marks and copyright, directly from the Controller General
It was converted into the Competition Appellate Tribunal in 2021
questions.e: Set up in 2003 under the Trade Marks Act, the board heard appeals against orders of the Registrar and the Controller. Its abolition shifted these appeals to the High Courts.
questions.s: Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Designs Act, 2000:
1. It protects the aesthetic features of an article, such as shape, pattern and ornamentation.
2. Registration is initially for 15 years, with no renewal.
3. It also protects the mode or principle of construction of an article.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A design is protected only for features that appeal to the eye, and the Act excludes the mode or principle of construction, which belongs to patents. Registration lasts 10 years, extendable by 5 years, for a total of 15.
questions.s: Designs Act, 2000

questions.q: The layout-designs of semiconductor integrated circuits are protected in India under the:
questions.e: India enacted a separate law to meet its TRIPS obligations on layout-designs, as these are neither ordinary inventions nor ordinary artistic works.
questions.s: SICLD Act, 2000; WTO TRIPS Agreement

questions.q: 'Evergreening' of patents refers to:
o: granting a compulsory licence to a generic maker after three years
extending the effective monopoly over a drug beyond the patent term by patenting minor modifications of an existing product
allowing the use of a patented product for regulatory trials before expiry
patenting plant varieties that stay green throughout the year
questions.e: Firms file fresh patents on new forms, doses or combinations to delay generic entry. Section 3(d) of the Indian Patents Act is designed to check this practice.
questions.s: Patents Act, 1970, Sec 3(d)
